title: CLIP-Style Symmetric Contrastive Loss
prompt:
An interviewer gives you a batch of paired image and text embeddings and asks you to implement the CLIP-style symmetric contrastive loss. Row `i` in the image tensor matches row `i` in the text tensor. Build the full in-batch similarity matrix, treat its diagonal as the positive pairs, compute image-to-text and text-to-image cross-entropy losses, and average them. Be ready to explain why the loss is symmetric, how off-diagonal entries become in-batch negatives, and what normalization and temperature do.

For this executable practice version, implement `clip_contrastive_loss(image_embeddings, text_embeddings, temperature=0.07, normalize=True)` in PyTorch. Both inputs are floating rank-2 tensors with matching shape `(B, D)`; assume `B > 0` and `D > 0`. When `normalize` is true, L2-normalize every row, then compute `image @ text.T / temperature`. Preserve dtype, device, and autograd; do not mutate either input. Reject rank or shape mismatches and a non-positive or non-finite temperature. The evaluator does not require a redundant empty-batch check because positive dimensions are a stated precondition.

Source boundary: the interview report confirms the paired-batch setup and the two cross-entropy terms over the similarity matrix and its transpose. The function signature, default temperature, optional normalization flag, and defensive validation are DeepCode conventions added to make the exercise reproducible.
